Why compounding knowledge beats raw intelligence

By Jane Reporter, May 10 2026

Most operators treat knowledge as a one-shot artifact. They read an article, take notes, and move on. The notes rot in a folder no one re-reads. Knowledge that does not compound is knowledge that decays.

The alternative is a system where every new piece of information attaches to entities and concepts that already exist. People, companies, ideas. Each new note strengthens the graph instead of orphaning itself.

This is the central claim Garry Tan made in his 2025 essay on second brains. The brain works because it gets read, not because it gets written. The output of a knowledge system is search hits and back-links, not document counts.

The practical implication for builders: invest in the entity resolution layer before you invest in the capture layer. Capture without resolution produces a swamp. Resolution without capture produces an empty graph. The two have to ship together.

It is fashionable to call this a "knowledge graph" but the term hides the actual mechanism. The mechanism is bidirectional links plus a notability gate. Everything else is plumbing.
